text:
olivia: Heads-up — noticed an unexpected line on the March invoice for accelerator commitments. rate for committed A100 pools appears to 'snap back' to on-demand for a subset of hours, and an extra 'support-bundle' line is duplicated for those same hours :thinking:

olivia: snippet from invoice CSV (redacted):
```
resource,usage_start,usage_end,sku,units,unit_price,charge
accelerator.a100,2024-03-12T00:00Z,2024-03-12T01:00Z,commitment-a100-pool,1,0.34,0.34
accelerator.a100,2024-03-12T01:00Z,2024-03-12T02:00Z,on-demand-a100,0.5,1.20,0.60
support.bundle,2024-03-12T01:00Z,2024-03-12T02:00Z,support-addon,1,0.10,0.10
support.bundle,2024-03-12T01:00Z,2024-03-12T02:00Z,support-addon,1,0.10,0.10
```

olivia: First line is committed rate, second hour is showing on-demand + two support lines for the exact same hour. sequence number and billing tags for those two support lines are identical.

matt: Ack — that's weird. Do we have a commit/usage mapping issue? Could be tag mismatch at the allocation layer. Can you paste the tag values?

olivia: tags look identical for the affected jobs: `client:redwood-inference`, `pool:dedicated-a100-4`, `commitment_id:cmt-58a3`. But for the on-demand hour the `charge_back_tag` is `null` in the billing export.

finance-bot: Automated alert: potential double-billing detected for invoice 2024-03-12 (support-addon). Confidence: 0.78. Related tickets: #BILL-7821

jia: @olivia thanks for flagging. From finance side, when `charge_back_tag` is null our reconciliation treats it as non-committed usage, which falls back to on-demand SKU. Why would `charge_back_tag` be dropped mid-period? Any deploys around that time?

ops-oncall: We had a rolling node replacement fleet job at 2024-03-12T00:45Z that drained a subset of pods. Could be that the drain triggered reattachment to ephemeral nodes without the tag propagation. Logs show controller applied `node.k8s.io/drain` to nodes a100-3 and a100-4 between 00:40-00:50Z.

glen: Two hypotheses: 1) tag propagation race during the drain, 2) cloud provider reclassified capacity when autoscaler replaced preemptible-backed instances. Which accelerators were used — preemptible/spot?

olivia: Affected jobs show `instance_preemptible=false` on commit lines, but the on-demand ones have `instance_type=ephemeral-gpu-tiebreaker`. Not obvious. Also support lines duplicated exactly — I suspect a billing system retry created duplicate support addon charge for the replaced instance.

matt: Can we query raw usage records from the provider for the hour 00:00-02:00 and compare allocation IDs? If allocation_id changes mid-hour that's likely cause. I'll run the provider export now.

matt: Quick dump: `alloc-112233` used until 2024-03-12T00:47Z, then `alloc-445566` from 00:47Z onward. Both map to same commitment id cmt-58a3 in our CP, but provider export lost the `commit` tag on alloc-445566.

jia: OK that's the smoking gun. Provider side lost the commit tag on the replacement allocation; reconciliation flagged that usage as on-demand and we ended up charging support-addon twice because the post-processing job retries appended support lines when reconciliation didn't find an existing commit match.

olivia: Action items: 1) block — prevent retries from emitting duplicate support lines if an identical support line exists for the same usage window (small fix in billing postproc). 2) ops — ensure tag propagation on node replacement path (controller needs to copy `commitment_id` to new alloc). 3) finance — run a correction for the affected invoice period.

matt: I'll open infra ticket to fix tag copy and add a metric to detect lost commitment tags in real-time. Ticket INFRA-1094. ETA: patch by EOD tomorrow.

ops-oncall: I'll add a preflight to the rolling script to stash tags and restore on new allocations. Also adding a post-drain audit that queries `billing_tags` for active allocations.

jia: Finance: we should estimate the overcharge and submit a refund request to provider or issue internal credits. Olivia, can you compile a list of affected lines (usage_start/charge) and rough delta?

olivia: Will do. Preliminary delta ~ $1,430 across 12 hours and 4 pools. I'll DM the CSV and create BILL-7845 for the correction request.

glen: For RCA doc: note the chain of events and timeline — drain -> allocation swap -> tag loss -> reconciliation fallback -> retry duplicate support emission. Recommend adding test for tag round-trip in our e2e upgrade tests.

olivia: Agreed. I'll write up the incident note in postmortems with timestamps and owner list. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
